final_answer: IMAGINE A VILLAGE WHERE EVERY SUMMER, ICE CREAM SALES AND MURDER RATES BOTH GO UP. A NON-SCIENTIST MIGHT SAY, “ICE CREAM CAUSES MURDERS!” BUT THIS IS A CORRELATION. NOW, IMAGINE WHAT HAPPENS IF THE VILLAGE GETS COLDER. ICE CREAM SALES DROP, AND MURDERS ALSO DROP. IF YOU THOUGHT “ICE CREAM CAUSES MURDERS,” YOU WOULD PREDICT LOWER MURDERS IN COLDER WEATHER. BUT IF YOU REALIZE THAT HOT WEATHER MAKES PEOPLE HUNGRY FOR ICE CREAM AND ALSO MAKES PEOPLE MORE AGITATED, YOU REALIZE THAT TEMPERATURE IS THE CAUSAL FACTOR. CORRELATION SAYS “THEY MOVE TOGETHER”; CAUSATION ASKS, “WHAT PUSHES THEM?” THE ANSWER OFTEN HIDDEN IS A THIRD VARIABLE (HOT WEATHER) THAT DRIVES BOTH. THIS IS WHY SCIENTISTS USE EXPERIMENTS TO ISOLATE CAUSE.
